items.q: A café sells 2,400 cakes a month at £3.50 each. What is its monthly revenue?
items.label: Calculate

items.q: A business has fixed costs of £8,000 a month. It makes 2,400 units, each with a variable cost of £4. What are its total costs?
items.why: Total variable costs = £4 × 2,400 = £9,600. Total costs = fixed costs + total variable costs = £8,000 + £9,600 = £17,600.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Revenue is £36,000 and total costs are £17,600. What is the profit?
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Fixed costs are £12,000. Each item sells for £20 and has a variable cost of £8. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Break-even = fixed costs ÷ (selling price − variable cost) = £12,000 ÷ (£20 − £8) = £12,000 ÷ £12 = 1,000 items. £12,000 ÷ £20 = 600 forgets the variable cost.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: The business in the last question sells 1,450 items. What is its margin of safety?
items.why: Margin of safety = actual output − break-even output = 1,450 − 1,000 = 450 items. It is measured in units, not pounds.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: The business raises its price from £20 to £24. Its costs stay the same. What happens to its break-even output?
items.why: Each item now contributes £24 − £8 = £16. £12,000 ÷ £16 = 750 items. A higher price means fewer sales are needed to break even, but customers may buy fewer at the higher price.
items.label: Use it

items.q: A shop's sales rise from £50,000 in 2024 to £62,000 in 2025. What is the percentage change?
items.why: (£62,000 − £50,000) ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%. Dividing by the new figure gives 19.4%, which is wrong.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: Revenue is £180,000. Cost of sales is £135,000 and other expenses are £32,400. What is the net profit margin?
items.why: Gross profit = £180,000 − £135,000 = £45,000. Net profit = £45,000 − £32,400 = £12,600. Net profit margin = £12,600 ÷ £180,000 × 100 = 7%. 25% is the gross profit margin.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: A machine costs £50,000. Over 5 years it brings in £80,000 in total. What is the average rate of return?
items.why: Total profit = £80,000 − £50,000 = £30,000. Average annual profit = £30,000 ÷ 5 = £6,000. ARR = £6,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 12%. 32% forgets to take off the cost of the machine.
items.label: Calculate

items.q: In March a business has an opening balance of £4,500. Cash inflows are £18,000 and cash outflows are £21,200. What is the closing balance?
items.why: Net cash flow = £18,000 − £21,200 = −£3,200. Closing balance = £4,500 + (−£3,200) = £1,300. −£3,200 is the net cash flow, not the closing balance.
items.label: Calculate
